name: MonarchEmailVerificationBanner
title: EmailVerificationBanner
wrapsNative: MonarchCalloutBanner with MonarchButton actions in a androidx.compose.foundation.layout.FlowRow, a LaunchedEffect countdown and a polite live region
summary: A notice that the email address is not verified yet, with the address, a Resend button that waits out a cooldown, and an optional Change email button.
whenToUse: While a signed-in person has not verified their email address, or after they changed it and the new one is not verified.
whenNotToUse: On the verification screen itself, where entering a code is the task, use MonarchOtpPinInput. For general notices use MonarchCalloutBanner.
api: @Composable fun MonarchEmailVerificationBanner(email: String, onResend: suspend () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, tone: MonarchTone = MonarchTone.Warning, placement: MonarchCalloutBannerPlacement = MonarchCalloutBannerPlacement.Section, cooldownSeconds: Int = 60, initialCooldownSeconds: Int = 0, onChangeEmail: (() -> Unit)? = null, onDismiss: (() -> Unit)? = null, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, dismissIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchEmailVerificationBannerLabels = MonarchEmailVerificationBannerLabels())

class MonarchEmailVerificationBannerLabels(title: String? = null, message: ((email: String) -> String)? = null, resend: String? = null, resendIn: ((seconds: Int) -> String)? = null, sent: String? = null, changeEmail: String? = null, dismiss: String? = null, error: String? = null)

options.name: email
options.description: The address waiting for verification, shown in the message.

options.name: onResend
options.description: Sends the email again. Throwing shows the error from labels and starts no cooldown.

options.name: tone
options.description: Warning when features are locked until verified; Info when nothing is blocked yet. Other tones draw as Warning.

options.name: placement
options.description: A rounded callout in the content, or a full-width strip at the top of a screen.

options.name: cooldownSeconds
options.description: Seconds before another send after a successful one.

options.name: initialCooldownSeconds
options.description: Seconds already remaining when the banner appears, for example right after sign-up sent the first email.

options.name: onDismiss
options.description: Shows a dismiss button. The banner does not hide itself; remove it here.

options.name: icon
options.description: An icon at the start in the tone color. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: dismissIcon
options.description: The close mark of the dismiss button. Without it the button shows "Dismiss" as text.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the title, the message, the button titles, the sent line, the dismiss name and the error.

states.name: sending
states.description: The resend button shows its progress indicator, reads "Loading" and ignores taps.

states.name: sent
states.description: "Verification email sent" in the success strong color, announced; the cooldown starts.

states.name: cooldown
states.description: The button reads "Resend in 42s", counts down every second and is disabled until 0.

states.name: error
states.description: "Couldn’t send the email. Try again." in the danger strong color, announced; Resend is available at once.

appearance: The surface of MonarchCalloutBanner: the subtle fill and border of the warning or info tone, rounded in a section, a strip with a line below on a page. Resend is a small secondary button, Change email a small ghost button; the status line uses the success strong or danger strong role. All roles come from the theme.
platformNotes: The parity map names MonarchBanner; the component is built on MonarchCalloutBanner instead, because it needs two actions and a page placement, as on iOS. The web exports useResendCooldown for other resend controls; on Android the cooldown is the internal MonarchResendCooldown, to be promoted if another component needs it. onResend is a suspend function run in the banner's coroutine scope. A failed send always shows the error from labels: Android exception messages are not written for people, so the thrown message is not shown (iOS shows a LocalizedError description). On the web the cooldown button keeps focus with aria-disabled; on Android it is disabled, which TalkBack still reads with the seconds left in its title. The web's landmark and actionPlacement props have no Android equivalent.
accessibility: The tone name, title and message with the address are one TalkBack element, as MonarchCalloutBanner reads them.
Resend, Change email and Dismiss are separate buttons with 48dp touch targets.
During the cooldown the resend button is disabled and its title says the seconds left.
"Verification email sent" and failures are announced through a polite live region and shown as text, not color alone.
edgeCases: Long addresses wrap inside the message.
The countdown runs while the banner is on screen; a banner removed and shown again starts from initialCooldownSeconds.
A send started while the banner leaves the screen is cancelled with it.

examples.title: Resend with a cooldown
examples.template:
MonarchEmailVerificationBanner(
    email = {{email}},
    onResend = { /* call the service */ },
    cooldownSeconds = {{cooldownSeconds}},
    onChangeEmail = {},
)
examples.code:
MonarchEmailVerificationBanner(
    email = "sam@example.com",
    onResend = { /* call the service */ },
    cooldownSeconds = 20,
    onChangeEmail = {},
)

examples.title: Info tone as a page strip
examples.code:
MonarchEmailVerificationBanner(
    email = "ana@example.com",
    onResend = {},
    tone = MonarchTone.Info,
    placement = MonarchCalloutBannerPlacement.Page,
)
